# Golden-task baseline (W0.11)

**Recorded:** 2026-11-18
**Runner:** `cargo run -p phantom-core --example bench`
**Definitions:** `bench/tasks/{desktop,browser,files}.yaml` (20 each, generated by
`scripts/generate_bench_tasks.py`)
**Machine:** Windows, self-hosted dev run (not yet the CI Windows runner).

## Result

| Backend | Tasks | Pass | Fail | Skipped | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| files / CLI | 20 | **20** | 0 | 0 | Deterministic (write/mkdir/remove/exists/contains/equals). |
| browser | 20 | 0 | 0 | 20 | Live backend not enabled in this run. |
| desktop | 20 | 0 | 0 | 20 | Live backend not enabled in this run. |
| **Total** | **60** | **20** | **0** | **40** | |

Runner summary: **20 pass / 0 fail / 40 skipped** (of 60).
Machine-readable results: `docs/benchmarks/latest.json`.

The skipped tasks are not failures: they require a running LLM service and the
hidden-desktop/browser backends. Run them with:

```powershell
$env:PHANTOM_BENCH_LIVE = "1"
$env:PHANTOM_BENCH_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:50051"
cargo run -p phantom-core --example bench
```

## What this baseline does and does not prove

- **Proves:** the harness loads all 60 YAML tasks, validates their schema, and
  executes the 20 deterministic file/CLI tasks correctly (20/20).
- **Does not prove:** any desktop or browser success rate. The §1 functional
  gates (12/20 desktop on 3 runs, 18/20 browser) are **not yet measured**.
  They depend on the W0.0 hidden-desktop feasibility decision and W1/W2 work.
- The full section-1 release gates remain open in the goal state.

## CI

The Windows CI job should run the deterministic suite on every PR. The live
suite should run on a self-hosted Windows runner with an interactive session —
scheduled once the W0.0 spike selects the narrow vs. isolated-VM strategy.
